learn.hook: A tiny ant, a street dog, a big banyan tree — they all share the Earth with us!
points: All living beings — people, animals and plants — need food, water and a safe place to live.
We should never hurt, tease or throw stones at animals.
In summer, we can keep a bowl of water out for birds and street animals.
We should not break branches or pluck flowers and leaves for no reason.
Every creature has a job in nature. Even spiders and earthworms are helpful.

example.q: Some boys are throwing stones at a street puppy. What should Priya do?
steps: Think: the puppy can get hurt and feel scared, just like us.
Priya should not join in, and should ask the boys to stop.
She should tell a trusted adult, who can help the puppy.
example.answer: Ask them to stop and tell a trusted adult

learn.reallife: Many children in India keep clay bowls of water on balconies in summer for sparrows, pigeons and mynas.

games.title: Kind or unkind to living beings?
items: Keeping water out for birds in summer
Feeding a hungry street dog with an adult
Watering the plants
Watching birds quietly
Pulling a dog's tail
Breaking branches for fun
Throwing stones at birds
Stepping on ants on purpose

quiz.q: It is a very hot day. What can you do for the birds?
options: Keep a bowl of clean water on the balcony
quiz.explain: In hot weather, birds find it hard to get water. A bowl of water helps them.
quiz.mistake: Does not think about animals' needs

quiz.q: Your friend is pulling a cat's tail. What should you say?
options: Please stop, it hurts the cat
quiz.explain: Animals feel pain. We should be gentle with them.
quiz.mistake: Thinks animals do not feel pain

quiz.q: Why should we not pluck flowers for no reason?
options: Flowers grow back in one minute
Flowers are part of the plant and become fruits and seeds
quiz.explain: Flowers help plants make fruits and seeds. They also feed bees and butterflies.
quiz.mistake: Thinks flowers are only for decoration

quiz.explain: The peacock (Indian peafowl) is India's national bird.
The tiger is India's national animal. The elephant is the national heritage animal.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the national animal and heritage animal

quiz.explain: The banyan is India's national tree. Its branches grow roots that hang down to the ground.
quiz.mistake: Guesses a common or useful tree

quiz.q: A spider has made a web in a corner of the garden. Is the spider useful?
options: Yes, it catches flies and mosquitoes
quiz.explain: Spiders catch insects like flies and mosquitoes in their webs.

quiz.q: You see an injured bird on the road. What is the best thing to do?
options: Take it to school in your bag
Tell an adult, who can contact an animal helper or vet
quiz.explain: An adult can safely help the bird and call someone who treats animals.
quiz.mistake: Tries to handle an injured animal alone

teach.ask: Gappu sees a boy chasing a puppy. He asks: why should we be kind to animals and plants?
teach.praise: Tweet! Every living being deserves kindness, just like me!
teach.nudge: Do animals feel pain and fear like us?

learn.hook: Trees, rivers, birds and bees keep the Earth beautiful. How can we keep nature safe?
points: Nature gives us air, water, food, wood and medicines.
We protect nature by planting trees, not wasting water and not littering.
In the Chipko movement in the hills of Uttarakhand, villagers hugged trees to stop them from being cut.
The Bishnoi people of Rajasthan are known for protecting khejri trees and blackbucks.
World Environment Day is on 5 June. Van Mahotsav, a tree-planting festival, is held in the first week of July.

example.q: Why did the villagers in the Chipko movement hug the trees?
steps: The trees were going to be cut down.
The villagers needed the forest for wood, food, water and fodder.
By hugging the trees, they stopped the axes and saved the forest.
example.answer: To stop the trees from being cut and to save their forest

learn.reallife: Plant a sapling with your family and give it a name. Water it and watch it grow with you!

games.title: Protecting nature
items: Planting trees helps protect nature.
Trees give shade, fruits, homes for birds and clean air.
Throwing plastic into a river is harmless.
Plastic dirties rivers and harms fish and other animals.
In the Chipko movement, people hugged trees to save them.
'Chipko' means 'to stick' or 'to hug'.
World Environment Day is on 5 June.
It is celebrated across the world on 5 June.
Cutting all the trees in a forest is good for the animals there.
Animals lose their food and homes when forests are cut.
Switching off fans and lights when we leave a room helps the Earth.
Saving electricity means less fuel is burnt to make it.

items.text: Villagers hugged trees in the ___ movement.
The Bishnoi people protect the ___ tree.
Van Mahotsav is a festival of planting ___.

quiz.q: Which of these helps protect nature?
quiz.explain: Planting saplings adds trees that give shade, fruits and homes for birds.
quiz.mistake: Confuses harmful acts with helpful ones

quiz.q: What did people do in the Chipko movement?
options: Hugged trees to save them from being cut
quiz.explain: Villagers in the Uttarakhand hills held on to trees so they could not be cut.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what Chipko means

quiz.q: The Bishnoi people of Rajasthan are known for protecting which animal?
quiz.explain: Bishnoi communities protect blackbucks and khejri trees in the desert.
quiz.mistake: Guesses an animal not found in India

quiz.q: On which date is World Environment Day celebrated?
quiz.explain: World Environment Day is on 5 June every year.
quiz.mistake: Mixes it up with other special days

quiz.q: Why are forests important for animals?
options: They give animals food and homes
They have no use for animals
quiz.explain: Forests are habitats where animals find food, water and shelter.
quiz.mistake: Does not link forests with animal habitats

quiz.q: Which habit helps keep a river clean?
options: Washing plastic bags in it and leaving them there
quiz.explain: Garbage, paint and plastic make river water dirty and harm fish and other living things.
quiz.mistake: Thinks rivers can carry away any waste

quiz.q: Van Mahotsav is held in the first week of which month?
quiz.explain: Van Mahotsav, a week of planting trees, is held in the first week of July, when the rains begin in much of India.
quiz.mistake: Does not know when Van Mahotsav is held

quiz.q: Each of 4 children plants 2 saplings on Van Mahotsav. How many saplings are planted in all?
quiz.mistake: Adds 4 and 2 instead of making 4 groups of 2

teach.ask: Gappu's favourite tree is going to be cut down. He asks: why should we protect trees and nature?
teach.praise: Chirp chirp! Let us plant more trees and keep nature clean!
teach.nudge: What can children do to protect nature?
